items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: Adam Powell was leaving the -- he was the first Negro councilman in New York and he was leaving the council to go to Congress... And he threw his support behind Ben Davis

ctx.x: (Inaudible) during the war when you had a problem. What was that problem about you down in the Village? There seemed to be some problem that you were in the wrong company, or something. And there was always some kind of problem that you could never -- now, I never got into this because I was with Cab Calloway and I never heard much there. Politically or something?

Oh, yeah. I was involved in the entertainment committee to promote the campaigns of Ben Davis. Adam Powell was leaving the -- he was the first Negro councilman in New York and he was leaving the council to go to Congress, to be a Congressman. And he threw his support behind Ben Davis who was a popular figure in Harlem. Because see, many Negros who were popular with the public, some of them -- not many but some went over on the left side, like Paul Robeson. Paul Robeson -- people worshipped Paul Robeson and Ben…
famous cases of racial injustice in the 1930's. And he got famous that way and --
